aggressive_definition: Lethal prostate cancer, identified among men diagnosed with prostate cancer through follow-up for lethal outcomes.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Men with prostate cancer were followed through March 2011 for lethal outcomes (n = 114).
study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the Health Professionals Follow-up Study
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We included 1260 men who were diagnosed with prostate cancer after providing a blood sample in 1993-1995 and 1331 control subjects.
reason: Prediagnostic plasma vitamin D was evaluated in a prospective nested case-control study of incident prostate cancer. The abstract separately analyzes overall prostate cancer and lethal prostate cancer, making this an analysis of both general and aggressive incidence rather than a survival-only study.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Higher 25(OH)D levels were associated with a 57% reduction in the risk of lethal prostate cancer (highest vs lowest quartile: odds ratio = 0.43, 95% confidence interval = 0.24 to 0.76).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate explicitly concerns lethal prostate cancer based on prediagnostic vitamin D levels and comparison with controls, supporting an aggressive incident endpoint.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
